blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Every good talk starts with a good question. At work, we ask short questions all day: Do you have a minute? Does she work on Fridays? These questions are small, but they are very useful.

Yes/No questions with do and does are easy to make. You start with "Do" or "Does", then the person, then the verb: Do you speak English? Do we have a meeting today?

The answers are short too. "Yes, I do." or "No, I don't." You do not need long sentences. Take your time. Every sentence counts, and one good question can start a good conversation.

items.q: According to the text, how does every good talk start?
items.why: "Every good talk starts with a good question."

items.q: How do you start a Yes/No question in the text?
items.why: "You start with 'Do' or 'Does', then the person, then the verb."

items.q: What is a short answer to "Do you speak English?"
options: Yes, I speak it very well and every day.
items.why: A resposta curta para "Do you...?" é "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't."

items.q: The text suggests that the writer would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: "A good question can start a good talk."
"You need long sentences to answer a question."
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "You do not need long sentences" — então discordaria dessa frase.

items.q: "Take your time" at the end suggests that you should…
items.why: Inferência: "Take your time" significa ir com calma, sem pressa.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emma praticando perguntas simples. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! I am Emma. I work at Czarnikow. Today I want to practise easy questions with you. They are short and very useful at work.

Listen. I ask: Do you work at Czarnikow? And you answer: Yes, I do. Or: No, I don't. It is easy. The answer is short.

Here is another one. Do you speak English? Maybe you say: Yes, I do. A little. That is fine. A little is good.

Now a question about time. Do we have a meeting today? I look at my calendar. No, we don't. We have a call tomorrow at nine. So today is calm.

I like coffee, so I ask a friend: Do you like coffee? She says: Yes, I do! We take a break and we talk. A small question, a nice break.

One more. Do you need help? This is a kind question. When you ask it at work, people feel good. So please, ask it often. Thank you for your time. See you soon!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does Emma work?
items.why: "I am Emma. I work at Czarnikow."

items.q: When Emma asks "Do you speak English?", what answer does she say is fine?
items.why: "Maybe you say: Yes, I do. A little. That is fine."

items.q: Do they have a meeting today?
options: No, they don't; they have a call tomorrow
items.why: "Do we have a meeting today? ... No, we don't. We have a call tomorrow at nine."

items.q: Emma suggests that asking "Do you need help?" is a good idea because…
options: it is only for the boss
it makes people feel good at work
it takes a long time to answer
it is a very hard question
items.why: Inferência: "This is a kind question... people feel good. So please, ask it often."

items.q: How would you best describe Emma's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ela é calma, gentil e diz "That is fine", "Thank you", "See you soon".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "That is a good question. Let me think." A question is…
items.why: Question = pergunta.

items.q: "I have your answer: yes, we can meet on Monday." An answer is…
items.why: Answer = resposta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Do you work here? ___, I do."
items.why: "Yes, I do" é a resposta afirmativa curta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Do we start at nine? ___, we don't. We start at ten."
items.why: "No, we don't" é a resposta negativa curta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Can you help me, ___?"
items.why: Please = por favor, usado para pedir com educação.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem em conversas curtas no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Do you have a minute?" This means…
options: Do you have a little time now?
items.why: "Do you have a minute?" = você tem um minutinho / um tempo agora?

items.q: "Let's take a break and have some coffee." To take a break means to…
options: stop work for a short rest
items.why: Take a break = fazer uma pausa curta.

items.q: A friend asks "Do you need help?" A polite answer is "Yes, please." This means…
options: Yes, I would like help. Thank you.
items.why: "Yes, please" = sim, por favor: aceita com educação.

items.q: Someone asks "Do you like coffee?" You say "No, thanks." This means…
options: I like tea only in winter
No, but thank you for asking
items.why: "No, thanks" = não, obrigado(a): recusa educada.

items.q: At the end of a chat, Emma says "See you soon!" This means…
options: Goodbye, we will meet again soon
items.why: "See you soon" = até logo / a gente se vê em breve.
